red_flags.title: Solar ITC forfeiture absent documented physical-work BOC by Jul 4, 2026 — ~$45.6M face loss
red_flags.evidence: Deadline has passed. Under OBBBA §70512 amending IRC §48E, solar facilities not beginning construction by Jul 4, 2026 (or PIS by Dec 31, 2027) receive $0. Notice 2025-42 eliminated the 5% safe harbor for >1.5 MWac — only documented physical work of a significant nature counts. On $202M capex with ~$152M solar basis, the lost credit is ~$45.6M face (~$0.25/Wac, 22.5% of capex), requiring +$3–5/MWh PPA uplift to hold returns. Post-deadline options: (1) storage-only ITC under §48E (storage exempt from the cliff; 30% through 2033, phase-down 2034–35); (2) transferability of the surviving storage credit under §6418; (3) domestic-content/energy-community adders on the storage tranche only. None restore the solar credit.
red_flags.benchmark: Full-credit case: $60.6M face / $53.3–57.0M transferred cash; missed-BOC case: $15M (KB split) to $19–34M (market turnkey basis) storage-only ITC — net swing $26–46M
sources: KB: RAI Solar A financials — ITC cliff kill-variable

red_flags.title: Storage-only ITC fallback requires basis segregation and FEOC-compliant BESS supply chain
red_flags.evidence: The surviving credit attaches only to energy storage technology basis. KB project split implies ~$50M BESS basis → ~$15M ITC; market turnkey for 320 MWh at $200–350/kWh implies $64–112M basis → $19–34M. The $202M/180 MWac = $1.12/Wac figure is PV-only scope — if the 80/320 BESS is inside $202M the project is $40–70M short and the ITC basis split is wrong. Separately, OBBBA's material-assistance cost ratio (Notice 2026-15) zeroes even the storage credit if cells/modules come from prohibited foreign entities (CATL/BYD effectively excluded), constraining integrator selection and cost.
red_flags.benchmark: BESS turnkey $200–350/kWh (2025–26 US market); realistic combined capex $240–280M vs stated $202M
sources: KB: financials benchmark — $1.12/Wac plausible only as PV-only EPC

red_flags.title: Transferability monetization haircut and compliance costs on surviving credits
red_flags.evidence: §6418 transferability survived OBBBA and is the monetization path absent tax-equity appetite, but credits clear at $0.88–$0.94 per $1.00. On the full $60.6M grandfathered credit that is a $3.6–7.3M discount plus 1.5–3% for transfer insurance/indemnity; on the storage-only fallback ($15–34M) the discount is $0.9–4.1M. Transfers are one-time, cash-only, post-PIS elections, and transferees cannot be specified foreign entities — buyer diligence and recapture indemnities (5-year ITC recapture period) must be priced into the model.
red_flags.benchmark: Transfer pricing $0.88–0.94/$1.00; insurance 1.5–3% of credit value
sources: KB red-flag checklist: tax-credit monetization haircut priced

red_flags.title: Continuity safe harbor leaves thin schedule margin to the Dec 31, 2030 PIS backstop
red_flags.evidence: Even with a valid 2026 BOC, the continuity safe harbor requires PIS by Dec 31, 2030. Q4 2029 COD fits with ~12 months cushion, but the KB flags interconnection as the second kill-variable: cluster study must complete ~mid-2027 and network-upgrade allocation vs the $24M trigger is unresolved; GSU transformer lead times run 128–144 weeks. Slippage past 2030 forfeits even a grandfathered credit; a missed-BOC project has no such protection at all on the solar tranche.
red_flags.benchmark: 4-year continuity window (Notice 2025-42); transformers 128–144 weeks; NV cluster study ~mid-2027 for Q4 2029 COD
sources: KB: interconnection kill-variable; supply-chain lead-time table

rfis: Site control: provide executed lease/option agreements, title reports or commitments, and legal access easements for all 1,080 acres; site control gates NV Energy Order 2023 cluster entry and is currently only assumed.

CAPEX scope: state explicitly whether the $202M EPC + owner cost figure includes the 80 MW / 320 MWh BESS; provide an itemized breakdown ($/Wac PV, $/kWh BESS, gen-tie, interconnection, owner costs). KB estimates $240-280M all-in, a $40-70M gap.

BOC / tax credits: produce all evidence of beginning of construction on or before Jul 4, 2026 under OBBBA / IRS Notice 2025-42 (binding contracts, 5% safe-harbor payments, physical work); if none exists, state the tax-credit assumption embedded in the FINANCE 75/100 score and stress claim.

Financial model: deliver the full model with targeted offtake price ($/MWh), revenue stack, tax assumptions, and stress cases; reconcile the +10% CAPEX stress ($20.2M) against the document's own $24M interconnection re-run trigger and the 8% equipment escalation reserve.

Offtake: provide status of PPA negotiations, counterparties (NV Energy IRP procurement, NRS 704B exit customers, data-center bilaterals), term sheets, and the targeted offtake price, which is never stated.
Interconnection: provide the application, queue position, cluster study status, any upgrade cost estimates, and the basis for assuming gen-tie-only feasibility with no study or executed agreement.
Gen-tie corridor: provide the route map with parcel-level land ownership and an analysis of any BLM land crossing, including ROW/NEPA exposure.
Boulder City development agreement: provide the draft agreement, the city's process steps, and a realistic timeline to execution within the 2026-2027 window.

Surveys: provide desert tortoise protocol survey results, Class III cultural survey, geotechnical report, and drainage/flood study; confirm whether the ~$0.6M MSHCP fee (~$550/ac x 1,080 ac) is carried in owner costs.

Procurement: provide GSU/main transformer quotes, confirmed lead times, and reservation status; provide BESS supplier quotes and delivery slots. The 24-month trigger contradicts the 30-36 month market norm.
Resource data: provide the bankable P50/P90 solar resource and yield report; none exists.
Construction water: identify the counterparty, contract terms, and water-rights source for temporary construction water.
Decommissioning: provide the decommissioning plan and bonding cost assumptions; none are stated.

Authorship and data provenance: provide signatures and preparer names, and reconcile the p. 4 disclaimer that parcel boundaries, economics, schedules, and counterparties are synthetic - identify which figures are real and which are placeholder.
Demand support: provide the quantitative Southern Nevada load-growth data supporting DEMAND 81/100, the highest factor score, given no offtake and no interconnection.
Escalation reserve: justify the 8% equipment reserve against the 10-15% prudent benchmark and the $24M single-risk trigger.

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability (DES) - Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan (MSHCP) program
agency_actions.action: Enroll the project for MSHCP incidental-take coverage, confirm desert tortoise survey requirements, and budget the ~$550/acre mitigation fee (~$0.6M on 1,080 ac); mobilize USFWS-protocol tortoise surveys immediately for the Sep-Oct 2026 window.
agency_actions.why: Tortoise coverage surveys gate layout freeze; the document's Q4 2026 start misses the Sep-Oct 2026 protocol window, costing ~6 months. Acting now (mobilization by early Sep 2026) preserves the schedule; the fee is not visibly carried in owner costs.
agency_actions.deadline: Surveyor mobilization by 2026-09-08 for the Sep-Oct 2026 window; MSHCP enrollment before layout freeze (Q2 2027)

agency_actions.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Nevada Fish and Wildlife Office (Reno)
agency_actions.action: Coordinate desert tortoise protocol surveys and determine the consultation path: ESA Section 7 if a BLM federal nexus exists (gen-tie ROW), otherwise Section 10 coverage via the Clark County MSHCP.
agency_actions.why: Desert tortoise is federally listed; the consultation path drives both the survey scope and the federal permitting timeline that the 2027-2028 environmental review window may not accommodate.
agency_actions.deadline: Path determination by Q4 2026; surveys Sep-Oct 2026 or spring 2027

agency_actions.agency: Bureau of Land Management - Southern Nevada District Office (Las Vegas)
agency_actions.action: Hold a pre-application meeting and, if the gen-tie crosses BLM land, file a FLPMA Title V right-of-way application (SF-299) and initiate NEPA review consistent with the 2024 Western Solar Plan.
agency_actions.why: Local precedent (Townsite Solar 2) shows ~2-3 years for BLM ROW + NEPA plus IBLA appeal risk; this is incompatible with a Q4 2029 COD unless started immediately or an all-private-land route is substituted.
agency_actions.deadline: Pre-application meeting Q4 2026; ROW application Q1 2027

agency_actions.agency: Boulder City Community Development Department and City Council
agency_actions.action: Initiate the development agreement process, obtain written parcel-level confirmation of the Energy Resource zoning designation, and map the approval path and duration for a non-city entity.
agency_actions.why: The development agreement is unexecuted and required before construction authorization; the process and timeline are undescribed and must fit the 2026-2027 window to support COD Q4 2029.
agency_actions.deadline: Initiate Q4 2026; execute development agreement by Q3 2027

agency_actions.action: Obtain a determination on Utility Environmental Protection Act (UEPA, NRS 704.820-704.900) applicability and, if applicable (generating facilities >= 70 MW), file the UEPA siting permit application.
agency_actions.why: UEPA/PUCN siting-cert applicability is unresolved; a 180 MW facility presumptively requires a PUCN permit, and the statutory review (~6 months) must be sequenced before construction.
agency_actions.deadline: Applicability determination Q1 2027; application filed by Q2 2027

agency_actions.agency: NV Energy - Transmission Planning (PUCN-regulated; FERC Order 2023 cluster process)
agency_actions.action: Submit the cluster interconnection application with site-control evidence for the Eldorado/Marketplace-Mead hub and request the cluster study schedule and upgrade-cost framework.
agency_actions.why: Site control is a cluster-entry gate and is currently unverified; the application-to-COD window (30-36 months) is ~2 years aggressive versus the ~5-year request-to-COD norm, and upgrade costs are unknown against the $24M re-run trigger.
agency_actions.deadline: Q4 2026-Q2 2027 application window, contingent on site control by Q4 2026

agency_actions.agency: Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP) - Bureau of Water Pollution Control
agency_actions.action: Obtain coverage under the Construction Stormwater General Permit (NVR100000) and prepare the SWPPP.
agency_actions.why: Required before any ground disturbance on a 1,080-acre site; not currently in the permitting plan.

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Department of Air Quality (DAQ)
agency_actions.action: Obtain a construction dust control permit for the site and access roads.
agency_actions.why: Clark County requires dust control permits for large disturbance areas in the Las Vegas Valley airshed; absent from the current permit matrix.

agency_actions.action: Confirm the water-rights source and obtain any temporary permits needed for construction water.
agency_actions.why: The construction water contract counterparty and terms are unspecified; water availability in the Eldorado Valley requires a permitted source.

agency_actions.action: Complete Section 106 consultation (if a BLM federal nexus exists) and SHPO review of the Class III cultural resources survey.
agency_actions.why: Cultural surveys are incomplete and gate layout freeze; Section 106 runs with the BLM NEPA review and carries the same schedule risk.

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Regional Flood Control District
agency_actions.action: Commission and obtain approval of the drainage study and flood hazard review for the site.
agency_actions.why: No geotech, drainage, or flood studies exist; flash-flood exposure in the Eldorado Valley affects layout, civil design, and insurability.
agency_actions.deadline: Study commissioned Q1 2027; approval by Q1 2028

agency_actions.agency: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), coordinated with Boulder City Municipal Airport (BVU)
agency_actions.action: Run a glare analysis (ForgeSolar/SGHAT) per FAA solar-on-airports policy and file any required Notice of Proposed Construction (Form 7460-1).
agency_actions.why: The site is in the Boulder City airport influence area; unassessed glare or airspace issues can force layout changes after freeze.

Boulder City: obtain written confirmation of parcel-level Energy Resource zoning and the development-agreement process steps and typical duration.

Gen-tie: corridor land ownership verified; if any BLM crossing, a filed ROW application with a NEPA schedule compatible with COD, or a committed all-private-land alternative route.

Schedule re-baseline: revised COD reflecting the ~5-year interconnection norm, 30-36 month transformer lead times, and BLM/NEPA exposure (realistically 2030-2031), or documented mitigation (pre-design transformer reservation by Q1 2027, accelerated cluster treatment).
Transformer reservation: binding GSU reservation placed by Q1 2027 with a delivery date before COD; the document's own 24-month trigger is already breached by market norms.
Development agreement: executed agreement with Boulder City and written parcel-level zoning confirmation before construction authorization.
Environmental: completed tortoise protocol and Class III cultural surveys, MSHCP enrollment with the ~$0.6M fee budgeted, and a USFWS consultation path (Section 7 or Section 10) confirmed.

UEPA: PUCN determination on UEPA applicability and, if required, a filed application with a decision timeline compatible with construction start.
Water and civil: executed construction water contract with a permitted source, plus completed geotech, drainage, and flood studies.
Decommissioning: approved decommissioning plan with bonding cost carried in the model.

Data integrity: signed, attributed diligence document with all synthetic figures (parcels, economics, schedules, counterparties) replaced by verified data; no IC reliance on the p. 4 synthetic dataset.
